study: N24: Cross-platform npm lockfile repair without unrelated version churn
source: FSE2027_4_ideas(2).zip/ideas/N24.md; exploratory B0001 is prior evidence, not confirmatory
scope: Public npm packages, reproducible npm-induced faults, and dated real GitHub lockfile snapshots

hypotheses.H1: A locked npm10 warm-regeneration defect can cause npm-ci success with a failing native loader on an unmatched platform
hypotheses.H2: An exact-version leaf-only donor repair restores correct native execution while making zero changes to unrelated locked versions
hypotheses.H3: Repair on already-correct locks and deliberately unsafe/unsupported graphs does not change dependencies
hypotheses.H4: The in-place current-npm and full-clean-regeneration baselines may match or outperform leaf-only repair; this is reported even if it negates a method claim

latest_npm_strong_baseline: 12.2.3 (registry latest on 2026-11-18; added before any npm12 run)
platforms: macos-15 arm64 or macos-15-intel x64 (record actual runner)
observational_unit: package family x actual host platform x fault; strategies are paired within each unit; seed repeats are not independent projects
stats: Report all denominators and 95% Wilson CIs for proportions, and exact paired differences; do not imply statistical significance from 3 OS or repeated seeds
holdout: Real historical lockfile snapshot mining is descriptive, not ground truth for CI failures without matching original CI logs
early_stop: If a supported npm version in-place fixes every tested case with no additional unrelated changes and lower/equal cost, do not claim an advantage for targeted repair
data_ethics: Do not execute untrusted lifecycle scripts; do not call simulated faults natural incidents; preserve independent source/version/provenance in artifacts
